_about: Reviewed linguistic data (fil.nouns.phrases): set phrases of the Quran taught on their noun's card — a studied noun and the adjective that follows it as one name. `ar` is the phrase in the nominative with full harakat, `adjective` the corpus lemma|root of the following word; the places are found in the corpus, never typed. `picture` names a studied noun whose picture stands beside the phrase. Every entry says why.

مَسْجِد|سجد.why: The mosque around the Kaaba in Mecca: مَسْجِد with the adjective حَرَام (sacred, inviolable) is one name, 15× in the Quran (2:144 … 48:27). Bosnian follows Korkut's term for it (Časni hram, 2:144, 17:1); English the usual name. The Kaaba stands in it, so its picture is shown beside the phrase.
